Consult Summary:
Adult with known eczema presents via telehealth with a 3-day worsening, widespread, itchy, dry erythematous rash on chest, arms, hands, and antecubital fossae. No systemic features; treated with emollients but needs stronger therapy.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Worsening eczema flare (past few days)
- Location: chest, hands, arms, especially antecubital fossae.
- Symptoms: sore, red, very itchy, dry; cracked areas; no weeping, no thickened skin.
- Pertinent negatives: no fever, no joint pains.
- Current self-care: Diprobase emollient cream daily; Dermol wash in shower; OTC hydrocortisone cream.
- Exam (telehealth): no direct visualization documented.
- Plan: start topical Betnovate (betamethasone) thin layer BID x 2 weeks; add oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine); continue emollients; monitor for response or adverse effects; follow-up if no improvement or worsening.

Issue 2: Asthma (intermittent, mild)
- Uses blue reliever inhaler (salbutamol) PRN only during flares.
- Currently asymptomatic; breathing normal.

Issue 3: Family history of migraine and hypothyroidism (mother) – relevance noted for future care.

Medications:
- Diprobase cream – dose/route/frequency not documented (patient uses daily).
- Dermol shower emollient – dose/route/frequency not documented (daily in shower).
- Hydrocortisone cream OTC – dose/route/frequency not documented (ineffective).
- Salbutamol (blue) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (PRN).
- NEW: Betnovate cream – apply thinly BID for 2 weeks.
- NEW: Fexofenadine – dose/route/frequency not documented (antihistamine).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Atopic eczema.
- Asthma.

Social History:
- Lives in London; further social history (smoking, alcohol) not discussed.

Preventative History:
- Not addressed in this consult.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person examination; no vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Send electronic prescription for Betnovate cream and Fexofenadine to patient’s nominated Boots pharmacy.
- Continue existing emollients (Diprobase, Dermol).
- Apply Betnovate thinly twice daily for 14 days.
- Take Fexofenadine as directed for itch.
- Return sooner if rash worsens, adverse reaction occurs, or no improvement after 2 weeks.
- Routine follow-up if needed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: smoking status, alcohol intake, vaccination/preventive screening history, medication doses/frequencies, objective skin exam or photographs, vitals.
● Internal conflicts: Patient states mother has “hypothyroidism”; clinician repeats “hyperthyroidism” (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor overlapping speech, no major inaudible sections.
